notes: Scores are relative indices from 0 to 100 that support decisions. They are not probabilities, and they do not certify landing safety.
Every threshold below is a documented assumption. Each was chosen for regional screening on the ~3.7 km MOLA MEGDR 16 ppd baseline. None is an established landing requirement.
Each factor uses a piecewise-linear function. q = 1 at or beyond `full` in the preferred direction. q = 0 at or beyond `zero`. Between the two, q changes linearly.

landing-v1.1 (2026-11-14): the solar_illumination `full` value moved from 185 to 178 W/m2, so that q = 1 can be reached (see that factor's rationale). The default weights, every other threshold and both default hard constraints are the same as in landing-v1.0.

criteria.label: Terrain safety (regional slope)
criteria.rationale: Lower regional slopes make it less likely that a landing ellipse covers tilted terrain, such as crater walls or rises. The 2 deg full-marks value and the 10 deg cut-off are screening assumptions on the ~3.7 km baseline. Recent landing-site selections set slope limits at much shorter baselines. InSight required slopes <15 deg at 84 m and 2 m length scales (Golombek et al., 2017). MSL required slopes <30 deg at 2-5 m baselines (Golombek et al., 2012). MEGDR 16 ppd slopes (~3.7 km baseline) cannot show slopes at these scales.

criteria.label: Elevation suitability (EDL atmosphere)
criteria.rationale: Lower elevation means more atmosphere above the site to slow the spacecraft during entry, descent and landing. MSL required an elevation <-1 km (Golombek et al., 2012). InSight required an elevation <=-2.5 km (Golombek et al., 2017). For Perseverance, new EDL capabilities meant that elevation and latitude limits no longer decided which sites were viable (Grant et al., 2018). The -3000 m and +2000 m values are a screening assumption that covers this range. +2 km is also the preliminary elevation limit for human Exploration Zones (Bussey & Hoffman, 2016). The real limit for a mission depends on its EDL system.

criteria.label: Surface roughness (detrended relief)
criteria.rationale: Standard deviation of MOLA elevation within the footprint, after a best-fit plane is removed. Low values show smooth plains at the km scale. High values show crater rims, scarps or hummocky terrain. The thresholds are assumptions. They were set so that smooth plains score near 1 and footprints dominated by crater walls score near 0. This value does not stand in for rock abundance or decimetre-scale roughness.

criteria.label: Thermal conditions
criteria.rationale: Warmer mean surface temperatures make thermal management easier for landed hardware. This is a placeholder. No Mars site has this value in profile v1, because THEMIS/TES data is not added yet. Under the common_feature_set policy, this factor is left out and reported as missing instead of scored.

criteria.label: Solar illumination (annual mean, top of atmosphere)
criteria.rationale: Annual-mean sunlight at the top of the atmosphere, calculated from latitude and the orbital elements of Mars (see SCIENTIFIC_METHOD.md). The thresholds are the physical range of this value in the pipeline's model (scripts/geo.py). The equatorial annual mean is 178.6 W/m2 and the polar annual mean is 79.8 W/m2. So `full` = 178 gives an equatorial site full marks, and `zero` = 80 gives a polar site zero. An earlier value of 185 W/m2 was S_Mars/pi = 186.6 W/m2 without obliquity. No latitude reaches that value, so q = 1 was impossible. This was corrected on 2026-11-14. The value ignores dust in the atmosphere and the local horizon. It is a latitude-based stand-in for available solar power, not a surface measurement.

default_hard_constraints.rationale: Assumption: footprints with a median elevation above +2 km leave too little atmosphere for current EDL systems. Past mission limits were lower. This is a generous screening limit.

Assumption: the 2015 NASA First Landing Site / Exploration Zone Workshop for human missions limited candidate zones to within 50 degrees of the equator, for solar power and thermal reasons. It is used here as a documented default. It is not a rule for robotic landers.

missing_data_policy.description: If a factor is missing for any site, it is left out for all sites. This way, every ranked score uses the same set of factors. The weights are rescaled over the remaining factors. If fewer than two factors remain, the status is insufficient_data. Missing values are never replaced with zero or an estimated number.
